translink_tsg_2018.title: TransLink, Transit Service Guidelines 2018 (public summary), 3.1 Vehicle Capacity Reference Table

notes: Routes in public/data/internal/dispatch/transit.json come from notebooks/dispatch_transit.py run on this feed. The feed covers 2026-09-07 to 2027-01-03, not July 2026; a representative weekday (2026-10-07) stands in for the typical weekday schedule. It is a static schedule, not real-time.

gtfs.licence_note: TransLink open data, used under TransLink's Transit Data Terms of Use (https://www.translink.ca/about-us/doing-business-with-translink/app-developer-resources). Not an official TransLink product.

bus_capacity.quote: Standard Bus — Average Seated Capacity 35, Average Practical Capacity 50

max_load.quote: Conventional 40-foot Bus: 36 seats, maximum passenger load of 77

bus_capacity.note: Practical capacity is used for planning replacement buses; the maximum load is the crush ceiling.

layover_min.unit: minutes per end of a replacement-bus round trip
layover_min.note: TransLink's guidelines exclude recovery (layover) time from running time but give no figure; 10 minutes per end is a team assumption.

rail_note.text: Rail (SkyTrain, West Coast Express) and ferry (SeaBus) rows describe the normal scheduled service to each home area. They are not something buses replace one-for-one; replacement-bus sizing uses bus_capacity only.
